target.title: ci(cloudflare): deploy crawl-remote from protected ClawSweeper environment
target.body:
## Summary

- split crawl-remote production deployment into an unprivileged preflight runner and a fresh protected deployment runner
- authorize any requested full SHA that remains an ancestor of current crawl-remote `main`, preserving idempotent fresh-dispatch resume while keeping workflow reruns forbidden
- build and test the exact target SHA without production credentials, then upload only the prebuilt Worker bundle, sanitized Wrangler config, D1 migrations, and a canonical SHA-256 manifest
- verify the bounded artifact, run/attempt/SHA/rollout-state identity, immutable action pins, production resource identities, and single-use receipt before mutation
- install exact Wrangler `4.107.1` in an isolated prefix with lifecycle scripts disabled before the Cloudflare token is exposed; the protected job never checks out or executes target npm scripts
- add validated `observation_order_state` selection (`dormant` or `active`) and bind it through artifact identity, receipt, strict D1 fence proof, and semantic production polling
- deploy with `CRAWL_REMOTE_RELEASE_SHA` set to the approved target SHA, retry stale HTTP 200 responses until the deadline, and require exact release identity plus capability absence for dormant or presence for active

## Security boundary

- preflight has no GitHub environment or Cloudflare credential and mints only an exact-repository `Contents: read` App token for `openclaw/crawl-remote`
- deploy runs under `crawl-remote-production` on a fresh runner with `bash --noprofile --norc`, cleared shell startup channels, no target checkout, and no target lifecycle/test execution
- `actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-node`, App token creation, artifact upload, and artifact download are immutable SHA-pinned and structurally asserted
- the only Cloudflare secret reference is the environment-specific `CRAWL_REMOTE_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, scoped to the migration/deploy step; there is no repository-secret fallback
- the verified config is stripped of `main` and `build`, cannot preconfigure the release SHA, and is locked to the expected Worker, route, D1 database, and R2 bucket

## Validation

- `node --test test/crawl-remote-deploy-workflow.test.ts test/actions-checkout-v7.test.ts` (15/15)
- executable adversarial coverage for artifact tampering, extra files, cross-state reuse, oversized files, strict D1 types/state, stale release identity, and malformed capability contracts
- ShellCheck on every workflow `run` block
- `pnpm run lint:scripts`
- `pnpm run format:check`
- `git diff --check`
- exact crawl-remote PR #35 head `19f5e01e250bc6ce2a75ee4b6ef0a26642f6be2b`: typecheck, 73 tests, Wrangler dry-run, dormant and active artifact package/verify, and prebuilt `--no-bundle` dry-runs
- Node 24 `pnpm run check`: active-surface, limits, build, and lint pass; root tests are 933/934 with the unchanged pre-existing `test/sweep-workflow.test.ts:1120` coverage-proof-tail failure. Repair tests (723/723) and changed coverage pass separately.
- pushed head `93bb74c5de99de22e09bb688c37a687402eb8ae3`: GitHub `CI/pnpm check`, both CodeQL analyses, Windows launcher coverage, and activity integration all pass

## Rollout

1. Land a crawl-remote release containing PR #35's public `release_sha` and dormant/active capability contract.
2. Before the first deployment, separately bootstrap `CRAWL_REMOTE_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` as an environment secret on `crawl-remote-production`. Do not create a repository fallback.
3. Restrict that custom Cloudflare token to account `91b59577e757131d68d55a471fe32aca` and zone `openclaw.ai`: Account Settings Read, Workers Scripts Edit, Workers R2 Storage Edit, D1 Edit, Workers Routes Edit for the zone, User Details Read, and Memberships Read.
4. The environment is already reviewer-protected and restricted to `main`, but currently has no environment secrets or variables.
5. Dispatch the first rollout with `observation_order_state=dormant`. After the operator changes the D1 cutover fence, future post-cutover releases dispatch with `observation_order_state=active`.
6. Use a fresh dispatch to resume an ancestor release after a partial failure; do not rerun an existing workflow attempt.

target.title: fix(review): keep maturity labels out of issue lease revisions
target.body:
## Summary
- exclude ClawSweeper-managed `maturity:stable` from issue source-revision hashing
- preserve ordinary label, protected label, and `proof: override` revision changes
- add focused regression coverage for the review-start lease key

This keeps ClawSweeper's own advisory maturity labeling from invalidating an in-flight exact-head review-start lease. It does not weaken `freshExactHeadReviewStartLease`, change pull-request head-SHA coordination, or alter unrelated label semantics.

Context: the exact-head source-revision lease path came from https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/501, and the managed maturity label came from https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/372. Thanks @yetval for the report and live timeline.

## Validation
- `node --test test/review-comment-rendering.test.ts`
- `pnpm run check`

Closes https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/issues/507
